tagline: Creek roads and old barns on the east edge of Columbus.
intro: Out past Gahanna a few township roads keep a rural character amid the subdivisions, Clark State Road and Reynoldsburg-New Albany Road and Kitzmiller Road among them. The cities have annexed much of Jefferson Township, and what is left rises and dips along Rocky Fork, Blacklick and Swisher creeks, with older barns and houses, many from the early 1800s, among the streams and stands of trees.
Native Americans named Blacklick Creek for the animals they saw coming to lick its black stones.

moments.title: Montei Indian Mound
moments.text: Local people knew this mound as Murder Hill or Hook's Hill, after tales of a one-armed man said to have lived there, and it now carries the name of its owner.

moments.title: Toll Keeper's House
moments.text: Built in 1832, the house kept the tolls when Clark State Road was the main way out to Newark, Johnstown and Granville.

moments.title: Kitzmiller Road
moments.text: The road hugs Blacklick Creek, most likely because two or three water mills once stood along it, and the miller is still there in its name.
